issues.legal_issue: A ceiling authority may examine the genuineness and bona fides of an alleged tenancy transfer when determining whether land should be counted in a landholder’s ceiling holding.
material_facts: In proceedings to determine the family unit’s agricultural landholding, the landholder sought to exclude land said to have been transferred to tenants under the tenancy legislation.
Tenancy authorities had made orders conferring tenancy rights and issuing certificates to the tenants.

The ceiling authority found the claimed tenancies unjustified and found that the transfers were not bona fide and had been made in anticipation of the ceiling legislation; it declared part of the land surplus.
The revenue tribunal and High Court upheld the ceiling authority’s determination.
issues.conclusion: The ceiling authority had jurisdiction in the ceiling proceedings to determine whether the alleged transfers were genuine and bona fide, including whether they were made in anticipation of the ceiling law. The challenge was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The tenancy legislation assigned tenancy-status questions to the tenancy authorities under section 100 and restricted civil-court jurisdiction under section 124. But the ceiling authority, when implementing the Maharashtra Agricultural Land (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961, could determine whether an alleged transfer creating a tenancy was genuine or was made to defeat the ceiling law; that inquiry is distinct from deciding whether tenancy rights were acquired under the tenancy legislation. The two enactments should be read complementarily to avoid frustrating their socio-economic purposes. The Court relied on the preamble to the Ceiling Act and Article 39(b) and (c) of the Constitution. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.ceiling_proceeding: A landholding is being assessed under a law that limits the amount of agricultural land a person or family unit may hold.
predicates.alleged_tenancy_transfer: A landholder claims, or another party alleges, that land was transferred by creating a tenancy.
predicates.transfer_purpose_relevant_to_ceiling: Whether the alleged transfer was genuine or was made to avoid the landholding limit is relevant to deciding which land counts toward the holding.

issues.definition: When a landholding-limit proceeding concerns an alleged tenancy transfer whose genuineness or purpose affects the land counted, the ceiling authority may assess the transfer for that proceeding.
